steps.subject: Revert "[SelectionDAG] Expand CTTZ_ELTS[_ZERO_POISON] and handle splitting" (#188220)

evidence: This is a revert of a prior CTTZ_ELTS legalization change after unrelated target ISel crashes.
It removes rather than introduces the relevant vector legalization path, and no evidence ties either the reverted feature or its reported crashes to X86 low-bit BT combining.
features: cttz-elements, meta:core-llvm, meta:revert, path:llvm/include/llvm/CodeGen, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/TargetLoweringBase.cpp
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Reverts the generic CTTZ_ELTS[_ZERO_POISON] legalization expansion: it removes TargetLowering::expandCttzElts and its legalization dispatches, and restores SelectionDAGBuilder's earlier target-controlled expansion using shouldExpandCttzElements. This restores builder-time construction of the SETCC/extension/reduction sequence for targets that request expansion.
Changed symbols: SelectionDAGBuilder::visitIntrinsicCall; TargetLowering::expandCttzElts; DAGTypeLegalizer::SplitVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntegerOperand; VectorLegalizer::LegalizeOp; VectorLegalizer::Expand; TargetLowering::expandVectorFindLastActive
Behavioral change: Removes legalization-time expansion and split/promotion support for CTTZ_ELTS and CTTZ_ELTS_ZERO_POISON.; Restores SelectionDAGBuilder's shouldExpandCttzElements gate, so expansion is again decided while lowering the intrinsic rather than unconditionally deferred to vector legalization.; Restores the previous builder-side SETCC, SIGN_EXTEND, AND, VECREDUCE_UMAX, subtraction, and ZEXT-or-TRUNC expansion sequence when the target requests expansion.; Removes the generic legalization-time type-promotion logic and i1-legal-operation preservation implemented by the reverted change.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; TargetLowering
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk identifies the reduced C testcase, -O1 behavior, X86 instruction selection, or the reported assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAGBuilder; SelectionDAG vector legalization; TargetLowering
Causal explanation: The candidate directly removes a prior broad SelectionDAG legalization change, including its extension/truncation and type-adjustment behavior. As a revert, it could eliminate a problematic DAG shape introduced by that prior implementation, but the supplied evidence does not say that it fixes this issue or that the reported crash involved CTTZ_ELTS. It also does not touch the X86 DAG-combine helpers named in the assertion. Thus the connection is indirect and this change is more plausibly a potential mitigation of the reverted feature than a demonstrated cause of the X86 low-bits failure.
Causal confidence: 0.11

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Optimize 32-bit udiv with 33-bit magic constants on 64-bit targets (#181288)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change modifies SelectionDAG unsigned-division expansion so that scalar i32 divisions may use a widened i64 magic-number sequence on targets that legalize/custom-lower i64 MULHU or UMUL_LOHI. TargetLowering::BuildUDIV now permits the magic-divisor computation to request widening, zero-extends the i32 dividend to i64, performs a 64x64-to-128 high-half multiply, and truncates the high i64 result back to the original result type. The commit adds X86 tests showing the new x86-64 mulq/mulxq code sequences and updates existing X86 urem expectations.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::BuildUDIV
Behavioral change: Allows scalar i32 unsigned-division magic-number lowering to select a widened i64 implementation when i64 MULHU or UMUL_LOHI is legal/custom.; Introduces an explicit i32-to-i64 ZERO_EXTEND, high-half 64x64 multiplication, and i64-to-result-type TRUNCATE path when the computed magic divisor requests widening.; Changes expected x86-64 code generation for affected constant udiv/urem cases from 32-bit magic-multiply adjustment sequences to widened 64-bit multiply sequences.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; The new path explicitly creates ZERO_EXTEND and TRUNCATE width adjustments, which is thematically aligned with the reported assertion text: "low bits constraint must survive width adjustment".; No retrieved hunk mentions peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, or the assertion itself.
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise x86_64 and i386 constant udiv/urem lowering, but no reduced C reproducer or -O1 crash regression test is present.; The new widened implementation is specifically tested on x86_64, the target family of the reported crash.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG TargetLowering; X86 code generation
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate among the retrieved commits because it adds precisely the sort of integer-width transition implicated by the assertion: an i32 value is widened to i64 and later truncated after arithmetic. Those nodes can alter the DAG seen by later X86 DAG combines. However, the patch changes generic BuildUDIV lowering rather than the named X86 combine routines, and the retrieved evidence does not establish that the reproducer contains constant unsigned division or reaches the new widened path.
Causal confidence: 0.55
Build risk: The path is guarded by target legality/custom-lowering checks for i64 MULHU or UMUL_LOHI, limiting it to targets supporting those operations.; New and updated X86 assembly tests cover x86_64, BMI2 x86_64, and i386 output for representative constant divisions and remainders.; No assertion/crash regression test for the reported low-bits constraint is included in the retrieved hunks.

+; Test optimization of 32-bit unsigned division by constants with 33-bit magic
+; constants (IsAdd=true) on 64-bit targets. The optimization uses pre-shifted
+; constants and 64x64->128 bit multiplication to reduce instruction count.

+; X64-NEXT:    movq %rdx, %rax

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth to look through ISD::FREEZE between a masking/truncating operation and a load. It preserves the freeze around the narrowed result, conditionally emits AssertZext or AssertSext nodes to retain extension/range information, and handles multi-use freezes by either rejecting unsafe narrowing or replacing uses with the narrowed load. New X86 tests cover masked, truncation, zero-extension, sign-extension, and freeze/load combinations.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; ISD::FREEZE handling in reduceLoadWidth; DAG.ReplaceAllUsesOfValueWith; ISD::AssertZext; ISD::AssertSext; and_freeze_load_i32_to_i8; and_freeze_load_i64_to_i8
Behavioral change: Allows reduceLoadWidth to recognize a LOAD through an intervening FREEZE, enabling narrowing of patterns such as AND(FREEZE(LOAD), low-bit-mask).; Preserves freeze semantics by rebuilding ISD::FREEZE around the narrowed result.; Introduces AssertZext or AssertSext after a freeze-preserving narrowed load so downstream DAG analyses retain knowledge of the result's extension/range constraint.; Avoids unsafe transformation through a multi-use freeze when other users require the original full-width load value, except for the specifically allowed anyext-to-zext adjustment.; Replaces all uses of the old load value for a qualifying multi-use freeze so users consistently see the replacement narrowed load.

Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth to look through ISD::FREEZE between a masking/truncating operation and a load. It preserves the freeze around the narrowed result, conditionally emits AssertZext or AssertSext nodes to retain extension/range information, and handles multi-use freezes by either rejecting unsafe narrowing or replacing uses with the narrowed load. New X86 tests cover masked, truncation, zero-extension, sign-extension, and freeze/load combinations.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; ISD::FREEZE handling in reduceLoadWidth; DAG.ReplaceAllUsesOfValueWith; ISD::AssertZext; ISD::AssertSext; and_freeze_load_i32_to_i8; and_freeze_load_i64_to_i8
Behavioral change: Allows reduceLoadWidth to recognize a LOAD through an intervening FREEZE, enabling narrowing of patterns such as AND(FREEZE(LOAD), low-bit-mask).; Preserves freeze semantics by rebuilding ISD::FREEZE around the narrowed result.; Introduces AssertZext or AssertSext after a freeze-preserving narrowed load so downstream DAG analyses retain knowledge of the result's extension/range constraint.; Avoids unsafe transformation through a multi-use freeze when other users require the original full-width load value, except for the specifically allowed anyext-to-zext adjustment.; Replaces all uses of the old load value for a qualifying multi-use freeze so users consistently see the replacement narrowed load.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAG combine; low bits constraint; integer width adjustment; sign-extension reasoning
Reproducer link: The new tests explicitly exercise low-bit masking and truncation of frozen i32/i64 loads, including AND masks of 255/65535/4294967295 and sign/zero-extension outcomes.; The reported crash occurs during X86 DAG instruction selection at -O1; this commit changes generic DAG-combine nodes and range assertions that can be consumed by later target-specific DAG combines.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG DAGCombiner; X86 SelectionDAG instruction selection; X86 CodeGen regression tests

Summary: This commit replaces the free llvm::isNeutralConstant predicate and SelectionDAG::getNeutralElement helper with SelectionDAG member APIs named isIdentityElement and getIdentityElement. The new predicate obtains the value's demanded-vector-elements mask and forwards it to an overload that can evaluate identity properties with demanded-element awareness; callers in DAGCombiner select folding and vector-reduction widening are migrated to the new APIs.
Changed symbols: llvm::isNeutralConstant; SelectionDAG::isIdentityElement; SelectionDAG::getNeutralElement; SelectionDAG::getIdentityElement; foldSelectWithIdentityConstant; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_VECREDUCE
Behavioral change: Identity-element recognition is moved from a free predicate to SelectionDAG::isIdentityElement.; The default identity check now computes getDemandAllEltsMask(V) and passes demanded vector elements into the identity analysis.; Floating-point constant/splat recognition in the migrated implementation receives the demanded-elements mask.; DAGCombiner select folding and vector-reduction widening use the new identity-element API.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit restructures SelectionDAG expansion of unsigned division and remainder by constants and adds a magic-number-based implementation for split wide values. It separates the previous decomposition helper from a new expandUDIVREMByConstantViaUMulHiMagic helper, computes unsigned-division magic parameters using known-leading-zero information, emits long multiply/add/subtract/shift DAG sequences, and adds extensive X86 code-generation tests for i64 and i128 constant udiv/urem cases.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandUDIVREMByConstantViaUREMDecomposition; TargetLowering::expandUDIVREMByConstantViaUMulHiMagic; TargetLowering::expandDIVREMByConstant; TargetLowering::expandMUL_LOHI; UnsignedDivisionByConstantInfo::get; DAG.computeKnownBits; udiv_i64_magic_large_postshift; urem_i64_magic_large_postshift
Behavioral change: Replaces the former monolithic unsigned div/rem-by-constant expansion path with separate decomposition and unsigned-multiply-high magic-algorithm helpers.; For eligible split unsigned UDIV/UREM operations with a nonzero, non-one constant divisor, computes magic-number pre-shift, multiplier, add-correction, and post-shift parameters.; Builds long arithmetic DAGs using BUILD_PAIR, UMUL_LOHI, UADDO/USUBO carry operations, FSHR, SRL, and reconstructed quotient/remainder values.; Uses known-leading-zero information from DAG.computeKnownBits to select a potentially reduced multiplier.; The visible implementation remains limited to unsigned constant division/remainder; the removed code explicitly rejected signed SDIV/SREM/SDIVREM.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAG combine; integer width reasoning

Summary: This change extends `LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1` from the documented v8i1/v16i1 scope to general vXi1 handling and adds a new lowering for BUILD_VECTOR masks with more than one non-constant i8 operand. When the derived byte and widened vector types are legal, it constructs a byte BUILD_VECTOR, performs an `ANY_EXTEND` to either byte or i32 elements depending on BWI support, masks each widened element with one, and compares against zero to recreate the i1 vector mask.
Changed symbols: LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; LowerBUILD_VECTORvXbf16
Behavioral change: Enables a new BUILD_VECTOR vXi1 lowering path for multiple non-constant i8 operands when the relevant vector types are legal.; Introduces an `ANY_EXTEND` followed by `AND 1` and `SETNE`, making the output mask explicitly depend on the low bit of widened byte or i32 elements.; Selects the widened element type based on `Subtarget.hasBWI()`: byte elements with BWI and i32 elements otherwise.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc and combineBTToBitOpFlag are not directly modified

Summary: This change rewrites the non-constant-lane handling in `LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1` to scalarize masks when all dynamic lanes use one distinct non-constant value. It then creates scalar selects with those immediate patterns, including split low/high i32 selects for v64i1, and inserts dynamic elements according to the lane mask.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Cast atomic vectors in IR to support floats (#148899)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds X86 IR-level casting of atomic loads with floating-point scalar element types to integer form, and adds X86 instruction-selection patterns for 128-bit atomic integer-vector loads. The accompanying tests update expected code generation for atomic float, half, and bfloat vector loads, generally replacing element-by-element reconstruction with direct vector moves.
Changed symbols: X86TargetLowering::shouldCastAtomicLoadInIR; TargetLowering::AtomicExpansionKind; atomic_load_128_v2i64; atomic_load_128_v4i32; atomic_vec1_bfloat; atomic_vec4_half; atomic_vec4_bfloat; atomic_vec4_float_align
Behavioral change: X86 returns AtomicExpansionKind::CastToInteger for atomic loads whose scalar element type is floating point, including floating-point vectors.; New TableGen patterns select 128-bit atomic integer-vector loads with MOVAPD/VMOVAPD-family register-memory moves when the relevant SSE2, AVX, or AVX-512 feature is available.; Atomic floating-point vector loads are expected to lower through integer-compatible atomic load handling and then be represented in XMM registers without reconstructing individual elements.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk connects the reduced -O1 C reproducer to atomic operations, atomic vector loads, floating-point vectors, or atomic IR expansion.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 target lowering; IR-level atomic expansion; X86 instruction selection
Causal explanation: The commit modifies X86 lowering and can alter the DAG entering instruction selection for atomic floating-point vector loads, but the retrieved changes do not touch peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, low-bit constraints, bit-test combines, or integer extension/truncation reasoning. The issue's reported assertion is therefore not directly supported by these hunks.
Causal confidence: 0.04
Build risk: The implementation and declaration changes are coordinated: X86TargetLowering::shouldCastAtomicLoadInIR is declared in X86ISelLowering.h and defined in X86ISelLowering.cpp.; The patch adds target-feature-specific atomic-load selection patterns for SSE2, AVX, and AVX-512.; X86 atomic-load regression expectations cover multiple floating-point vector types and both optimized and unoptimized configurations.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Reworks X86 SelectionDAG lowering of BUILD_VECTOR for i1 vectors. Rather than tracking nonconstant element indices and recognizing only a splat, the lowering tracks a nonconstant-element bitmask and distinct nonconstant values, scalarizes the single-nonconstant-value case into a select between computed true/false masks, adjusts all-ones-like extended masks for folding, handles v64i1 through separate i32 halves, and reinserts remaining nonconstant lanes from the bitmask.
Changed symbols: LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1
Behavioral change: Replaces NonConstIdx and IsSplat tracking with NonConstMask and a set of distinct nonconstant SDValues.; Generalizes the scalarized select case from a splat to any BUILD_VECTOR with exactly one distinct nonconstant element.; Builds select true and false operands from NonConstMask and the constant immediate instead of always selecting all-ones versus zero.; Adjusts a true immediate to an all-ones value at the selected scalar width when the vector true mask, accounting for undef lanes, is all ones.; For v64i1, forms separate low and high i32 selects, bitcasts each to v32i1, and concatenates them.; Reinserts nonconstant vector elements according to NonConstMask using DAG.getInsertVectorElt.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; integer-width adjustment; low-bits-related mask construction
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk includes the reduced C testcase, an -O1 invocation, or an assertion regression test.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; BUILD_VECTOR i1 lowering
Causal explanation: This is directly in the reported X86 SelectionDAG lowering subsystem and changes boolean-mask construction, bitcasts, i32/i64 splitting, undef handling, and an explicit width-dependent all-ones adjustment. Those features are plausibly capable of changing the DAG shapes and extension/truncation reasoning seen by later combines. However, the retrieved hunks do not modify peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag and do not directly establish that BUILD_VECTOR vXi1 reaches the asserted bit-test combine, so the connection is substantial but indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.52
Build risk: The change affects target lowering for i1 vector construction and introduces width-sensitive i64 mask arithmetic and v64i1 low/high splitting.; No test-file hunk or explicit assertion reproducer was retrieved for this commit, limiting direct validation evidence.

steps.subject: [X86] Fold XOR of VGF2P8AFFINEQB and its source (#198448)

evidence: Introduces a real X86 SelectionDAG combine, but only for GFNI affine-XOR vector operations.
No changed code matches peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, or the low-bits assertion.
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends the X86 SelectionDAG combine for GF2P8AFFINEQB so that an XOR of a GFNI affine operation with its original input can be folded into the affine operation by XORing the matrix rows with an identity matrix. It also refactors the XOR operand matching and adds X86 code-generation tests for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit GFNI cases, including guarded non-fold cases.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; test_affine_src_xor_fold_128; test_affine_src_xor_fold_256; test_affine_src_xor_fold_512; test_affine_src_xor_fold_alternative_matrix; test_affine_src_xor_nonzero_imm; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_multi_use; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_var_matrix
Behavioral change: Recognizes GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) XOR x when the matrix bits can be extracted as target constants.; Builds a replacement matrix whose rows are the original matrix rows XORed with the corresponding identity-matrix row, then returns a replacement GF2P8AFFINEQB node.; Changes the existing constant-splat path to inspect the newly matched XOR operand.; Adds tests for the new fold across vector widths and for cases that must remain unfolded, including multiple-use and variable-matrix cases.
Assertion or trace link: Matches X86ISelLowering.cpp; Matches X86 SelectionDAG combine logic; Uses APInt and target-constant extraction; No peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; No combineBTToBitOpFlag; No matching low-bits constraint assertion
Reproducer link: No retrieved evidence shows that the reported reduced C testcase produces GF2P8AFFINEQB operations or uses GFNI target features.; The added tests cover GFNI affine-XOR folds rather than the reported -O1 low-bits-constraint crash.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG combine; GFNI/GF2P8AFFINEQB target-specific lowering
Causal explanation: This is a genuine X86 DAG-combine behavior change, so it is closer to the implicated subsystem than the other candidates. However, the new logic is narrowly specific to vector GFNI affine transforms and constant matrix construction. The retrieved hunks contain no bit-position extension/truncation traversal, low-bit invariant update, or BT-to-flag combine logic, so the evidence supports only a weak indirect connection.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Introduces a new target-specific combine that constructs per-lane APInt constants and a BuildVector replacement node.; New CodeGen/X86 tests exercise 128-, 256-, and 512-bit folding behavior plus several intentional no-fold cases.; The change is feature-specific to GFNI/GF2P8AFFINEQB paths, limiting its apparent exposure outside those target patterns.

Summary: This commit extends the X86 SelectionDAG combine for GF2P8AFFINEQB so that an XOR of a GFNI affine operation with its original input can be folded into the affine operation by XORing the matrix rows with an identity matrix. It also refactors the XOR operand matching and adds X86 code-generation tests for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit GFNI cases, including guarded non-fold cases.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; test_affine_src_xor_fold_128; test_affine_src_xor_fold_256; test_affine_src_xor_fold_512; test_affine_src_xor_fold_alternative_matrix; test_affine_src_xor_nonzero_imm; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_multi_use; test_affine_src_xor_no_fold_var_matrix
Behavioral change: Recognizes GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) XOR x when the matrix bits can be extracted as target constants.; Builds a replacement matrix whose rows are the original matrix rows XORed with the corresponding identity-matrix row, then returns a replacement GF2P8AFFINEQB node.; Changes the existing constant-splat path to inspect the newly matched XOR operand.; Adds tests for the new fold across vector widths and for cases that must remain unfolded, including multiple-use and variable-matrix cases.
Assertion or trace link: Matches X86ISelLowering.cpp; Matches X86 SelectionDAG combine logic; Uses APInt and target-constant extraction; No peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; No combineBTToBitOpFlag; No matching low-bits constraint assertion
Reproducer link: No retrieved evidence shows that the reported reduced C testcase produces GF2P8AFFINEQB operations or uses GFNI target features.; The added tests cover GFNI affine-XOR folds rather than the reported -O1 low-bits-constraint crash.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG combine; GFNI/GF2P8AFFINEQB target-specific lowering
Causal explanation: This is a genuine X86 DAG-combine behavior change, so it is closer to the implicated subsystem than the other candidates. However, the new logic is narrowly specific to vector GFNI affine transforms and constant matrix construction. The retrieved hunks contain no bit-position extension/truncation traversal, low-bit invariant update, or BT-to-flag combine logic, so the evidence supports only a weak indirect connection.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Introduces a new target-specific combine that constructs per-lane APInt constants and a BuildVector replacement node.; New CodeGen/X86 tests exercise 128-, 256-, and 512-bit folding behavior plus several intentional no-fold cases.; The change is feature-specific to GFNI/GF2P8AFFINEQB paths, limiting its apparent exposure outside those target patterns.

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Widen <2 x T> vector types for atomic store (#197618)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends SelectionDAG vector type legalization to widen vector operands of ISD::ATOMIC_STORE. The new WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE obtains the widened stored value, finds a memory type preserving the original atomic memory width, coerces the widened scalar/vector value back to that type with bitcast/extract operations when necessary, and emits a replacement atomic store. X86 atomic-vector tests cover resulting code generation for small vector atomic stores.
Changed symbols: coerceStoredValue; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer
Behavioral change: Adds ISD::ATOMIC_STORE handling to vector-operand widening in the SelectionDAG type legalizer.; Preserves the original atomic memory width by selecting a FirstVT memory type and rebuilding the stored operand from the widened value.; For scalar FirstVT values, converts the widened value through a vector bitcast and extracts element zero; for vector FirstVT values, requires FirstVT to equal WidenVT.; Uses zero store alignment when finding the atomic memory type so legalization does not widen an atomic access beyond the object due to alignment.
Assertion or trace link: The change performs explicit width adjustment through WidenVT, FirstVT, TypeSize, BITCAST, and extract-vector-element operations.; The retrieved code does not mention peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, or the "low bits constraint must survive width adjustment" assertion.

Summary: Adds an X86 DAG combine that fuses a BT with a sibling bit-reset, bit-set, or bit-complement operation on the same source into a flag-producing BTR, BTS, or BTC node. The new combine peels truncation, zero/any-extension, and low-bit-preserving AND masks from bit positions to prove that the BT and modifying operation address the same hardware-masked bit; this peeling logic contains the reported low-bits width-adjustment assertion.
Changed symbols: peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; combineBT; X86btr; X86bts; X86btc; X86ISD::BTR; X86ISD::BTS
Behavioral change: combineBT now attempts combineBTToBitOpFlag before its prior BT-combine handling.; combineBTToBitOpFlag detects matching AND/OR/XOR bit-modifying users of a BT source and replaces the separate BT plus modification with one flag-producing BTR/BTS/BTC node.; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc strips TRUNCATE, ZERO_EXTEND, and ANY_EXTEND wrappers from bit positions and strips AND masks only when they preserve the low log2(bit-width) bits relevant to BT-family instructions.; After every stripped width-changing wrapper, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc asserts that the underlying value still has at least log2(BW) bits: "low bits constraint must survive width adjustment".; New instruction-selection patterns map the new BTR/BTS/BTC DAG nodes to 32-bit and 64-bit register instructions, and new tests cover masked, truncated, and zero-extended bit positions.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB - use getConstVector to create shuffle mask (#201122)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes X86 PSHUFB shuffle-mask construction in lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB. Instead of building a vector of SDValue constants/undefs directly, the code now records integer mask elements, represents zeroing lanes as 0x80 and undef lanes as -1, and materializes the mask through getConstVector(..., IsMask=true) before creating the X86ISD::PSHUFB node.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; X86ISD::PSHUFB
Behavioral change: PSHUFB masks are now represented as integer lane values and converted through getConstVector with mask semantics rather than assembled with DAG.getBuildVector.; Previously explicit DAG undef mask elements are represented by -1 for getConstVector, while zeroing lanes remain encoded by an i8 sign-bit value of 0x80.; The changed tests show a different constant-mask materialization/code-generation shape, using vpbroadcastq followed by register-mask vpshufb instead of immediate-looking shuffle-mask displays.
Reproducer link: The changed tests exercise vector shuffle/truncation cases, not the reported reduced C -O1 bit-test crash.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; X86 vector shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This commit does modify X86ISelLowering.cpp and constructs SelectionDAG nodes, so it is in the broad backend area of the failure. However, the retrieved change is confined to PSHUFB vector-shuffle mask construction. It does not touch combineBTToBitOpFlag, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, BT/BTR/BTS/BTC matching, integer bit-index width adjustment, or the reported low-bits assertion. The available evidence therefore provides no direct causal path to the assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: X86 code-generation tests were updated for AVX512F/AVX512VL shuffle output.; The semantic representation of undef and zeroing mask lanes changes, creating target-specific shuffle-regression risk.; No assertion-focused or BT-combine regression test is added by this commit.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Move Non-VLX handling for VPMADD52 instructions entirely into tablegen (#200800)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This X86 change moves non-VLX VPMADD52 handling from X86 DAG-combine eligibility checks into TableGen patterns. It broadens small-vector PMADD52 combine matching for IFMA-capable targets, removes a VLX rejection in matchVPMADD52, and adds NoVLX patterns that implement 128-bit and 256-bit operations by inserting values into 512-bit vectors, executing a ZMM VPMADD52 instruction, and extracting the original subregister width.
Changed symbols: matchVPMADD52; combineMulToPMADD52; VPMADD52LUQ; VPMADD52HUQ; avx512_pmadd52_common; test_mul_52bit_ymm; test_256_combine; test_128_combine
Behavioral change: Small v2i64 and v4i64 PMADD52 combines now accept HasIFMA without also requiring HasVLX.; The matchVPMADD52 path no longer rejects sub-512-bit vectors solely because VLX is unavailable.; For HasIFMA plus NoVLX, new TableGen patterns widen XMM/YMM operands into v8i64 ZMM values with INSERT_SUBREG and IMPLICIT_DEF, execute a 512-bit VPMADD52 operation, then narrow with EXTRACT_SUBREG.; The updated tests confirm that NoVLX 128-bit and 256-bit cases now produce ZMM VPMADD52 sequences rather than the prior multiply/add or VPMULLQ sequences.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: The changed paths explicitly alter 128-bit and 256-bit vector-width handling by widening through 512-bit ZMM values on NoVLX targets.; The included X86 CodeGen tests exercise the new width-adjusted PMADD52 lowering for v2i64 and v4i64 values.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG combine; X86 target lowering; X86 TableGen instruction selection
Causal explanation: This is the closest candidate because it directly changes X86ISelLowering SelectionDAG-combine eligibility and introduces explicit vector-width adjustment through INSERT_SUBREG and EXTRACT_SUBREG. Those facts make it relevant to an assertion concerning preservation of low-bit constraints across width adjustment. Nevertheless, none of the retrieved hunks touch peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, bit-test lowering, or the reported assertion itself; the edited combine is specifically for VPMADD52/IFMA vector arithmetic. Summary: This commit extends the X86 SelectionDAG OR combiner to fold an OR of a constant byte splat into GF2P8AFFINEQB even when the OR operands are not proven disjoint. It retains the existing disjoint-fold case, but for a constant matrix it instead clears matrix rows corresponding to forced-one output bits and ORs the splat into the GF2P8AFFINEQB immediate.
Changed symbols: combineOrWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; combineOr; test_or_disjoint_overlap_with_imm; test_affine_or_fold_v16i8; test_affine_or_fold_v16i8_mask33; test_affine_or_fold_v32i8; test_affine_or_fold_v32i8_mask33; test_affine_or_fold_512_v64i8
Behavioral change: The combiner now first matches an OR whose left operand is a one-use X86ISD::GF2P8AFFINEQB and whose right operand is a full constant splat.; For disjoint ORs, it preserves the prior fold of the splat into the GF2P8AFFINEQB immediate using XOR.; For non-disjoint ORs with a fully constant affine matrix, it creates a replacement matrix with rows zeroed for output bits forced by the splat and creates a new GF2P8AFFINEQB with immediate Imm | Mask8.; combineOr now invokes combineOrWithGF2P8AFFINEQB as an additional X86 DAG-combine transformation.

Summary: This commit extends the X86 SelectionDAG OR combiner to fold an OR of a constant byte splat into GF2P8AFFINEQB even when the OR operands are not proven disjoint. It retains the existing disjoint-fold case, but for a constant matrix it instead clears matrix rows corresponding to forced-one output bits and ORs the splat into the GF2P8AFFINEQB immediate.

Summary: Changes X86 lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB to construct PSHUFB control masks as integer lane values and materialize them through getConstVector(..., IsMask=true), rather than building a vector from per-lane DAG constants, undef values, and a shared 0x80 zeroing constant. The resulting PSHUFB and bitcast structure is otherwise retained, with test expectations updated for the new constant-mask materialization.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; X86ISD::PSHUFB
Behavioral change: PSHUFB shuffle-mask lanes are accumulated as integers, using -1 for undef lanes and 0x80 for lanes that must zero the output under PSHUFB semantics.; The mask is materialized by getConstVector with IsMask=true instead of DAG.getBuildVector over individual SDValue constants.; Generated code for the covered AVX-512 shuffle cases changes from inline shuffle-mask immediates to a broadcasted mask register reused by vpshufb instructions.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: The added/updated coverage concerns AVX-512 byte-vector shuffle and truncation patterns, not scalar bit-test-and-modify patterns.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; PSHUFB shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This commit does touch X86ISelLowering and SelectionDAG value construction, but its visible scope is PSHUFB vector-shuffle mask materialization. The reported assertion is in the BT fusion path's peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc width reasoning, and no BT/BTR/BTS/BTC combine, bit-position normalization, or low-bit-preservation check is changed here. The overlap is therefore only at the broad X86 DAG-lowering layer, not at the implicated algorithm.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Move Non-VLX handling for VPMADD52 instructions entirely into tablegen (#200800)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit moves no-VLX handling for narrow VPMADD52 operations from X86 SelectionDAG combine legality checks into TableGen patterns. The X86 combiner now permits 128- and 256-bit IFMA forms without requiring VLX, and new NoVLX patterns widen operands into ZMM subregisters, execute 512-bit VPMADD52, and extract the original XMM or YMM result.
Changed symbols: matchVPMADD52; combineMulToPMADD52; VPMADD52LUQ; VPMADD52HUQ; test_mul_52bit_ymm; test_256_combine; test_128_combine
Behavioral change: matchVPMADD52 no longer rejects sub-512-bit vector forms merely because AVX-512VL is absent.; combineMulToPMADD52 now treats v2i64 and v4i64 forms as supported when either IFMA or AVXIFMA is present, rather than requiring IFMA plus VLX for IFMA support.; For HasIFMA plus NoVLX, new TableGen patterns lower v2i64 and v4i64 x86vpmadd52l/h nodes by inserting XMM/YMM values into v8i64 operands, executing a 512-bit VPMADD52 instruction, and extracting the narrow subregister result.; Tests update no-VLX expectations from fallback multiply sequences to widened ZMM VPMADD52 instruction sequences.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG; DAG combine
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests cover IFMA/VPMADD52 vector multiply-and-add combines under AVX512 no-VLX configurations, not the reported O1 reduced testcase's bit-test path.; No retrieved hunk mentions the low-bits-constraint assertion, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, combineBTToBitOpFlag, or bit-test lowering.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG combine; X86 instruction-selection TableGen patterns
Causal explanation: The commit directly modifies X86 DAG-combine eligibility and the subsequent instruction-selection patterns, so it is in the same broad X86 SelectionDAG subsystem as the failure. Its actual logic is narrowly about selecting VPMADD52 for vector multiplication patterns and legalizing no-VLX narrow vectors through 512-bit subregister operations. The supplied evidence does not connect that vector IFMA path to the reported low-bit width-adjustment assertion in BT-related combining, so the candidate has only a low indirect risk.
Causal confidence: 0.13
Build risk: The combine now produces narrow VPMADD52 nodes for no-VLX IFMA targets that previously fell back to other lowering sequences.; Correctness depends on the new TableGen INSERT_SUBREG, VPMADD52, and EXTRACT_SUBREG patterns being selected for the intended NoVLX feature combination.; Updated X86 tests explicitly cover 128-bit and 256-bit no-VLX code generation and verify the widened ZMM instruction sequences.

The X86 combiner now permits 128- and 256-bit IFMA forms without requiring VLX, and new NoVLX patterns widen operands into ZMM subregisters, execute 512-bit VPMADD52, and extract the original XMM or YMM result.
behavioral_change: matchVPMADD52 no longer rejects sub-512-bit vector forms merely because AVX-512VL is absent.

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86InstrAVX512.td b/llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86InstrAVX512.td
index d8367412be58..34ea27a55d77 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86InstrAVX512.td
+++ b/llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86InstrAVX512.td
@@ -7231,0 +7232,29 @@ defm VPMADD52HUQ : avx512_pmadd52_common<0xb5, "vpmadd52huq", x86vpmadd52h,
+// Use 512bit VPMADD52LUQ/VPMADD52HUQ version to implement 128/256 bit in case NoVLX.
+let Predicates = [HasIFMA, NoVLX] in {
+  def : Pat<(v2i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR128X:$x, VR128X:$y, VR128X:$z)),
+            (EXTRACT_SUBREG
+             (VPMADD52LUQZr
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$x, sub_xmm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$y, sub_xmm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$z, sub_xmm)), sub_xmm)>;
+  def : Pat<(v2i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR128X:$x, VR128X:$y, VR128X:$z)),
+            (EXTRACT_SUBREG
+             (VPMADD52HUQZr
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$x, sub_xmm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$y, sub_xmm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$z, sub_xmm)), sub_xmm)>;
+
+  def : Pat<(v4i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR256X:$x, VR256X:$y, VR256X:$z)),
+            (EXTRACT_SUBREG
+             (VPMADD52LUQZr
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$x, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$y, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$z, sub_ymm)), sub_ymm)>;
+  def : Pat<(v4i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR256X:$x, VR256X:$y, VR256X:$z)),
+            (EXTRACT_SUBREG
+             (VPMADD52HUQZr
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$x, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$y, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$z, sub_ymm)), sub_ymm)>;
+}

top_candidates.subject: [CodeGen] De-type getMinimalPhysRegClass and related APIs (#197495)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit de-types TargetRegisterInfo minimal physical-register-class queries and updates SelectionDAG instruction emission and scheduling callers accordingly. The previous MVT- or LLT-sensitive APIs are replaced by an untyped virtual getMinimalPhysRegClass(MCRegister) query, and scheduler code no longer derives a physical register value type before asking for its register class.
Changed symbols: TargetRegisterInfo::getMinimalPhysRegClass; TargetRegisterInfo::getCommonMinimalPhysRegClass; InstrEmitter::EmitCopyFromReg; CheckForPhysRegDependency; ScheduleDAGFast::InsertCopiesAndMoveSuccs; ScheduleDAGFast::ListScheduleBottomUp; ScheduleDAGRRList::InsertCopiesAndMoveSuccs; ScheduleDAGRRList::PickNodeToScheduleBottomUp
Behavioral change: getMinimalPhysRegClass no longer accepts MVT or LLT type information and is made a pure virtual untyped physical-register query.; SelectionDAG instruction emission and scheduling now choose a minimal physical register class from the register alone rather than from the register plus the DAG value type.; The local getPhysicalRegisterVT helpers are removed from the fast and register-pressure schedulers because their results are no longer used for minimal-register-class selection.; Physical-register dependency copy-cost decisions now use the untyped minimal class.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: The retrieved changes concern post-selection instruction emission and scheduling register classes, not the O1 X86 DAG-combine bit-test reproducer.; No retrieved hunk mentions X86ISelLowering.cpp, combineBTToBitOpFlag, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, low-bits constraints, truncation, or sign extension.
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG instruction emission; SelectionDAG scheduling; TargetRegisterInfo
Causal explanation: This touches SelectionDAG infrastructure, but its shown behavior is limited to physical-register-class selection during instruction emission and scheduling. The reported failure is an X86 target DAG-combine assertion involving low-bit constraints and width adjustment, which is a different phase and mechanism. The retrieved hunks provide no evidence that this refactor changes the relevant X86 combine or integer-width reasoning, making it an unlikely cause.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Changing getMinimalPhysRegClass to a pure virtual untyped API requires all TargetRegisterInfo implementations and callers to conform; completeness outside the retrieved hunks cannot be verified here.; Removing type-dependent register-class selection can alter copy-cost and scheduling decisions for physical-register dependencies.; No test-file hunk was retrieved for this commit, so direct regression coverage is not visible in the supplied evidence.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB - use getConstVector to create shuffle mask (#201122)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change refactors X86 PSHUFB shuffle-mask construction in lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB: it replaces a vector of DAG SDValue constants, undef nodes, and a shared 0x80 zeroing constant with an integer mask vector passed to getConstVector as a mask. The resulting PSHUFB node is formed from that constant-vector result, and X86 shuffle tests are updated to expect materialized/broadcast mask vectors feeding vpshufb.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; PSHUFBMask; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8_1
Behavioral change: Represents PSHUFB masks as SmallVector<int> values rather than prebuilt SDValue constants or undef nodes.; Uses getConstVector(..., IsMask=true) to build the PSHUFB mask operand.; Changes tested AVX512VL code generation from embedded-looking shuffle masks to a vpbroadcastq-produced mask register consumed by vpshufb.
Assertion or trace link: X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: The added/updated coverage is for vector byte-shuffle lowering on AVX512 configurations, not the reported reduced C testcase crashing at -O1.; No retrieved hunk mentions BT, BTR/BTS/BTC, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, or a low-bits width-adjustment assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 SelectionDAG lowering; PSHUFB vector-shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This commit is in the broad X86 SelectionDAG-lowering area named by the issue, so it has some backend proximity. However, its visible algorithm concerns vector shuffle-mask materialization, whereas the failure signature is specifically in bit-test fusion and low-bit preservation across integer extension/truncation. The retrieved evidence supplies no direct control-flow or data-flow connection to that assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Touches X86ISelLowering.cpp and therefore can affect X86 instruction selection.; Has focused CodeGen/X86 tests for AVX512 shuffle output.; Visible test expectation changes confirm altered generated instruction shape for affected shuffle cases.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This SPIR-V backend fix changes integer-to-integer conversion opcode selection in generateConvertInst to use the source operand's signedness rather than the destination type's signedness. It adds SPIR-V OpenCL transcoding tests covering signed-to-signed, signed-to-unsigned, unsigned-to-signed, unsigned-to-unsigned, and integer-to-float conversion cases.
Changed symbols: generateConvertInst; IsSourceSigned
Behavioral change: For integer-to-integer OpenCL conversion builtins, chooses SPIRV::OpSConvert when the source type is signed and SPIRV::OpUConvert when the source type is unsigned.; Moves IsSourceSigned computation so it is available for the integer conversion opcode decision.; Adds code-generation and optional spirv-val coverage verifying that conversion extension behavior follows source signedness.
Pass or subsystem link: SPIR-V builtin lowering; SPIR-V CodeGen
Causal explanation: Although this change concerns signedness and width-extension semantics, the evidence places it exclusively in SPIR-V builtin lowering. The reported failure is an X86 SelectionDAG combine assertion involving BT bit-position peeling and preservation of low index bits. No X86, SelectionDAG combine, peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc, or combineBTToBitOpFlag code is changed here.
Causal confidence: 0.02
Build risk: Changes a target-specific C++ lowering implementation.; Adds focused llc regression coverage and an optional spirv-val validation run.; No X86 source or X86 test is modified in the retrieved hunks.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/CodeGen/SPIRV/transcoding/OpenCL/convert_signedness.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+; Check that convert_ builtins pick the signed/unsigned opcode from the source
+; operand signedness.
+
+; RUN: llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: %if spirv-tools %{ llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - -filetype=obj | spirv-val %}
+
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoS:]] "s_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoU:]] "s_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoS:]] "u_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoU:]] "u_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoF:]] "s_to_f"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoF:]] "u_to_f"
+
+; signed source -> signed dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> unsigned dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> signed dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> unsigned dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertSToF
+define spir_func void @s_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertUToF
+define spir_func void @u_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef)

+declare spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef)

Summary: This NFC LLDB change factors the existing L1 memory-cache range lookup out of MemoryCache::Read into a new MemoryCache::FindL1CacheEntry helper. The read path retains the same hit behavior—copying from a cache entry only when one entry covers the entire requested range—but obtains the data pointer through the helper.
Changed symbols: MemoryCache::FindL1CacheEntry; MemoryCache::Read
Behavioral change: Extracts the existing L1-cache lookup, containment check, and byte-offset calculation from MemoryCache::Read into FindL1CacheEntry.; MemoryCache::Read now treats a non-null helper result as an L1 hit and performs the same memcpy/return of dst_len as before.; The helper is documented to require that the caller holds m_mutex.
Pass or subsystem link: LLDB MemoryCache
